historical_references.reference: Thamer ibn Ashar, a notable warrior and general during the early Umayyad Caliphate. He is best known for his role in the conquest of Egypt in 639 AD, where he led the vanguard of the Muslim army against the Byzantine forces. Later, he was instrumental in the Muslim conquest of Damascus in 635 AD, which paved the way for the establishment of the Umayyad Caliphate.
historical_references.context: Early Umayyad Caliphate, Muslim conquests in Syria and Egypt

historical_references.reference: Thamer ibn Malik al-Qadahi, a medieval Islamic scholar and jurist. He is known for his contributions to the field of Islamic jurisprudence, particularly in the areas of inheritance and family law. Thamer was born in Kufa, Iraq, in the late 7th century AD and studied under prominent scholars such as Abu Hanifa and Ibrahim an-Nakhai. He was a prominent figure in the Hanafi school of Islamic law and his works continue to be studied and referenced in contemporary Islamic scholarship.
historical_references.context: Medieval Islamic scholarship, Hanafi school of Islamic law
